text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Ukrainian foreign minister Gennady Udovenko will begin a two- day visit to Estonia today by meeting President Lennart Meri.
- While investigating a mysterious noise at night, a Tallinn resident expecting to scare a burglar was frightened by his neighbour's two-metre spotted rock snake.

- A conference of the Unrepresented Nations and Peoples Organisation in Tallinn approved a statement that calls on the avoidance of violence but admits it is justified if a nation is defending itself against armed aggression or genocide.
- Chairman of Tallinn city council and the interior minister continue to accuse each other of political games after the recent dismissal of a senior police chief.
- Three percent of children aged 8-14 do not attend school and many interrupt their studies, statistics officials said.
- The public is being asked not to enter forests because of the risk of fire.
- The partially-built Tartu Baptist Church lost its roof in a fire on July 23. The pastor suspects arson.
- The Estonian government has not paid a private firm for building a Rescue Depot in Rapla, although the construction was finished in February.
